title: Aunt Marion starts him on piano
summary: Missing a mother's love but well cared for, Leeman starts piano at six or seven with his aunt and longs for drums, using his uncle's practice pad and homemade xylophone.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: As a child, I missed a mother's love, living with older people, my grandfolks, but I was treated beautifully and I had good schooling. I was never hungry. And my aunt took an interest -- she's still living, she's 91, she's an old maid.
I've met this lady, I'm proud to say.

Yeah, she's 91 and very alert. And she took an interest in me in the family, living there with my grandfolks. She started me on piano when I was 6 or 7 for about 2 years -- she was a wonderful teacher. And I
didn't go very far from there, but I did it. I did gain some musical knowledge by fooling around myself.

As I went through high school, I knew the keyboard and so forth -- I couldn't play any recital piano. Of course, I had my heart set on drums, because there was a pad around the house that my uncle had made at the Conservatory and in those days you made -- he made his own xylophone, and he was a thoroughly schooled drummer, he was a beautiful drummer, and to give up a career like that was unheard of. My aunt helped him through, that was her brother who helped him through college. But then he went to the Boston University and graduated and became an insurance executive -- and he had a very -- well, shall we say lucrative; he had a good life, and did some very good things with himself.
